arxiv-1501-05181.title: Isomorphy up to complementation
arxiv-1501-05181.creator: Maurice Pouzet, Hamza Si Kaddour
arxiv-1501-05181.description: A 2015 arXiv research paper by Maurice Pouzet, Hamza Si Kaddour. Considering uniform hypergraphs, we prove that for every non-negative integer h h there exist two non-negative integers k k and t t with k ≤ t k\leq t such that two h h -uniform hypergraphs ℋ {\mathcal{H}} and ℋ ′ {\mathcal{H}}^{\prime} on the same set V V of vertices, with | V | ≥ t |V|\geq t , are equal up to complementation whenever ℋ {\mathcal{H}} and ℋ ′ {\mathcal{H}}^{\prime} are k k -hypomorphic up to complementation.

arxiv-1908-07612.title: Accessing temperature waves: a dispersion relation perspective Journal: Journal of L a T e X Templates
arxiv-1908-07612.creator: Marco Gandolfi, Giulio Benetti, Christ Glorieux, Claudio Giannetti, Francesco Banfi
arxiv-1908-07612.description: Abstract © 2019. This manuscript version is made available under the CC-BY-NC-ND 4.0 license http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/ In order to account for non-Fourier heat transport, occurring on short time and length scales, the often-praised Dual-Phase-Lag (DPL) model was conceived, introducing a causality relation between the onset of heat flux and the temperature gradient.

arxiv-2011-13400.title: Phase-field modelling for fatigue crack growth under laser-shock-peening-induced residual stresses
arxiv-2011-13400.creator: Martha Seiler, Sören Keller, Nikolai Kashaev, Benjamin Klusemann, Markus Kästner
arxiv-2011-13400.description: Abstract For the fatigue life of thin-walled components, not only fatigue crack initiation, but also crack growth is decisive. The phase-field method for fracture is a powerful tool to simulate arbitrary crack phenomena. Recently, it has been applied to fatigue fracture. Those models pose an alternative to classical fracture-mechanical approaches for fatigue life estimation.

arxiv-2106-13845.title: Focusing Atom Laser Beams
arxiv-2106-13845.creator: R. Richberg, A. M. Martin
arxiv-2106-13845.description: Abstract We theoretically study the focusing of a quasi-continuous atom laser beam of rubidium-85 ( 85 Rb). A two-sate model analysis based on the Gross-Pitaevskii equation is used which comprises the effects of two-body atom-atom interactions and three-body recombination losses.

arxiv-2307-16764.title: Benchmarking of flatness-based control of the heat equation Thanks: Web: https://forschung.rwu.de/forschungsgruppen/control-and-process-engineering
arxiv-2307-16764.creator: Stephan Scholz, Lothar Berger, Dirk Lebiedz
arxiv-2307-16764.description: Abstract Flatness-based control design is a well established method to generate open-loop control signals. Several articles discuss the application of flatness-based control design of (reaction-) diffusion problems for various scenarios. Beside the pure analytical derivation also the numerical computation of the input signal is crucial to yield a reliable trajectory planning.

arxiv-2310-00943.title: S emi-Blind Image Deblurring Based on Framelet Prior
arxiv-2310-00943.creator: M. Zarebnia, R. Parvaz
arxiv-2310-00943.description: Abstract The problem of image blurring is one of the most studied topics in the field of image processing. Image blurring is caused by various factors such as hand or camera shake. To restore the blurred image, it is necessary to know information about the point spread function (PSF).

arxiv-2407-10376.title: Large Language Model-based FMRI Encoding of Language Functions for Subjects with Neurocognitive Disorder
arxiv-2407-10376.creator: Yuejiao Wang, Xianmin Gong, Lingwei Meng, Xixin Wu, Helen Meng
arxiv-2407-10376.description: Abstract Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) is essential for developing encoding models that identify functional changes in language-related brain areas of individuals with Neurocognitive Disorders (NCD). While large language model (LLM)-based fMRI encoding has shown promise, existing studies predominantly focus on healthy, young adults, overlooking older NCD populations and cognitive level correlations.

arxiv-2409-01686.title: Frequency-Spatial Entanglement Learning for Camouflaged Object Detection
arxiv-2409-01686.creator: Yanguang Sun, Chunyan Xu, Jian Yang, Hanyu Xuan ✉, Lei Luo ✉
arxiv-2409-01686.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yanguang Sun, Chunyan Xu, Jian Yang, Hanyu Xuan ✉, Lei Luo ✉. Camouflaged object detection has attracted a lot of attention in computer vision. The main challenge lies in the high degree of similarity between camouflaged objects and their surroundings in the spatial domain, making identification difficult.

arxiv-2410-00526.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Conversational Question Answering in Multi-instructional Documents
arxiv-2410-00526.creator: Shiwei Wu, Chen Zhang, Yan Gao, Qimeng Wang, Tong Xu, Yao Hu, Enhong Chen
arxiv-2410-00526.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Shiwei Wu, Chen Zhang, Yan Gao, Qimeng Wang, Tong Xu, Yao Hu, Enhong Chen. Instructional documents are rich sources of knowledge for completing various tasks, yet their unique challenges in conversational question answering (CQA) have not been thoroughly explored. Existing benchmarks have primarily focused on basic factual question-answering from single narrative documents, making them inadequate for assessing a model’s ability to comprehend complex real-world instructional documents and provide accurate step-by-step guidance in daily life.

arxiv-2505-11000.title: Neutron Spin Resonance Near a Lifshitz Transition in Overdoped Ba 0.4 K 0.6 Fe 2 As 2
arxiv-2505-11000.creator: Yang Li, Dingsong Wu, Yingjie Shu, Bo Liu, Uwe Stuhr, Guochu Deng, Anton P. J. Stampfl, Lin Zhao, Xingjiang Zhou, Shiliang Li, Amit Pokhriyal, Haranath Ghosh, Wenshan Hong, Huiqian Luo
arxiv-2505-11000.description: Abstract Elucidating the relationship between spin excitations and fermiology is essential for clarifying the pairing mechanism in iron-based superconductors (FeSCs). Here, we report inelastic neutron scattering results on the hole overdoped Ba 0.4 K 0.6 Fe 2 As 2 near a Lifshitz transition, where the electron pocket at M M point is nearly replace by four hole pockets.

arxiv-2508-01439.title: Theoretical Diagnostics for the Physical Conditions in Active Galactic Nuclei under the View of JWST
arxiv-2508-01439.creator: Lulu Zhang, Ric I. Davies, Chris Packham, Erin K. S. Hicks, Daniel E. Delaney, Miguel Pereira-Santaella, Laura Hermosa Muñoz, Ismael García-Bernete, Claudio Ricci, Dimitra Rigopoulou, Almudena Alonso-Herrero, Martin J. Ward, Enrica Bellocchi, Cristina Ramos Almeida, Francoise Combes, Masatoshi Imani
arxiv-2508-01439.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Lulu Zhang, Ric I. Davies, Chris Packham, Erin K. S. Hicks, Daniel E. Delaney, Miguel Pereira-Santaella, Laura Hermosa Muñoz, Ismael García-Bernete, Claudio Ricci, Dimitra Rigopoulou, Almudena Alonso-Herrero, Martin J. Ward, Enrica Bellocchi, Cristina Ramos Almeida, Francoise Combes, Masatoshi Imani. With excellent spectral and angular resolutions and, especially, sensitivity, the JWST allows us to observe infrared emission lines that were previously inaccessible or barely accessible. These emission lines are promising for evaluating the physical conditions in different galaxies.

arxiv-2509-20848.title: Actively Learning Halfspaces without Synthetic Data
arxiv-2509-20848.creator: Hadley Black, Kasper Green Larsen, Arya Mazumdar, Barna Saha, Geelon So
arxiv-2509-20848.description: Abstract In the classic point location problem, one is given an arbitrary dataset X ⊂ ℝ d X\subset\mathbb{R}^{d} of n n points with query access to an unknown halfspace f : ℝ d → { 0 , 1 } f\colon\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\{0,1\} , and the goal is to learn the label of every point in X X .

europmc-pmc7083237.description: Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations are the second most common oncogenic driver event in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Classical activating mutations (exon 19 deletions and the L858R point mutation) comprise the vast majority of EGFR mutations and are well...

pmc-11499496.title: Acute Cerebellitis Following COVID-19: Alarming Clinical Presentation Challenged by Normal Paraclinical Findings
pmc-11499496.creator: Samantha Poloni, Abdoulaye Hamani, Valentine Kassis, Pauline Escoffier, Beate Hagenkotter, Vincent Gendrin, Souheil Zayet, Timothée Klopfenstein
pmc-11499496.description: We report the case of an acute cerebellitis following COVID-19 in 32-year-old man who presented with a life-threatening critical cerebellar syndrome contrasting with normal paraclinical findings. Despite this fulminant critical presentation, the patient fully recovered in 37 days after early treatment with high-dose steroids and intravenous immunoglobulins.

pmc-11513053.title: Running in mice increases the expression of brain hemoglobin-related genes interacting with the GH/IGF-1 system
pmc-11513053.creator: Marion Walser, Lars Karlsson, Reza Motalleb, Jörgen Isgaard, H Georg Kuhn, Johan Svensson, N David Åberg
pmc-11513053.description: The beneficial effects of exercise are partly mediated via local or systemic functions of the insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) system. As IGF-1 increases local brain hemoglobin beta (Hbb) transcripts, we hypothesized that exercise could have similar effects. Mice were single-housed with free access to running wheels for seven days.

pmc-11794326.title: Padlet: a tool for fostering collaborative learning and feedback literacy in dental education
pmc-11794326.creator: Avita Rath
pmc-11794326.description: BackgroundWhile health professions education has embraced collaborative and co-creative learning approaches, the integration of digital technologies into feedback practices remains limited, especially in undergraduate dental education. This study investigated the impact of Padlet, a digital pinboard, on collaborative learning and feedback literacy among undergraduate dental students during a formative assessment activity guided by Nicol and MacFarlane's feedback principles.

pmc-12552703.title: The impact of PANoptosis-related genes on immune profiles and subtype classification in ischemic stroke
pmc-12552703.creator: Xinrui Cai, Yu Ren, Haiyun Wu, Yongjun Tan, Li Zhou, Yilin Wang, Qinghuan Yang, Jiani Wang, Hao Tang, Jun Wen, Yong Zhao, Ling Wang, Xinlei Xu, Jiagui Huang, Qin Yang
pmc-12552703.description: Ischemic stroke (IS) is an acute neurological disorder causing brain dysfunction, with high mortality and disability. PANoptosis is a synchronized sort of regulated cell demise that combines the characteristics of pyroptosis, apoptosis, and necroptosis. However, its role in ischemic stroke remains unclear.

pmc-12610717.title: Thermal Stability of Dexamethasone—Evaluation with Regard to Modern Medicinal and Pharmaceutical 3D-Printing Applications
pmc-12610717.creator: Roman Svoboda, Roman Vrbenský, Jan Honzíček, Mária Chromčíková, Giulio Malucelli
pmc-12610717.description: The high-temperature thermal stability of dexamethasone (DEX) was systematically investigated under nitrogen and air atmospheres using non-isothermal thermogravimetry at heating rates of 0.1–20 °C·min−1. The thermal decomposition was found to initiate below the melting temperature, proceeding via a three-step pathway that generated a complex mixture of volatile and condensed by-products (~10% solid residuum at 550 °C).

pmc-12648194.title: Role of Polyamines in Mitigating Salinity Stress in Ornamental and Food Crops
pmc-12648194.creator: Soheyla Mohammadi Alagoz, Behnam Asgari Lajayer, Zahra Azimzadeh, Younes Kheirizadeh Arough, Bernard Dell
pmc-12648194.description: Soil and irrigation salinity continue to have a major impact on the world's agriculture and horticulture, and loss of plant production is likely to worsen with global warming and climate change. Efforts to mitigate salinity stress and breed better salt‐tolerant plants rely on our knowledge of plant response to abiotic stress at the physiological and molecular levels.

pmc-12753892.title: Urantide alleviates lipopolysaccharide/D-galactosamine-induced acute liver failure through upregulating carboxylesterase1f in mice
pmc-12753892.creator: Wanhua Yang, Shu Bian, Liangming Liu
pmc-12753892.description: AimsTo investigate the effect of urotensin II(UII)/UII receptor(UT) on hepatic carboxylesterase1f(Ces1f) expression in acute liver failure(ALF) mice.MethodsALF was induced in male Balb/c mice using lipopolysaccharide (LPS)/D-galactosamine (D-GalN) i.p. after a tail vein injection of Urantide, a specific antagonist of UT receptor. Liver tissues were collected at 0-12h to detect UII and Ces1f mRNA levels in ALF mice.

pmc-13342330.title: Trends in primary brain tumour incidence and mortality in Ireland 1995–2019
pmc-13342330.creator: Kathleen Bennett, Bernadine O’Donovan, Stephen Macnally, Paul Carroll, Niamh Kavanagh, Ailish Malone, Frances Horgan
pmc-13342330.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundPrimary brain tumours are a source of mortality and morbidity which require extensive resources, diagnostic and therapeutic technology. There is evidence that people with brain tumours can benefit from rehabilitation, but frequently experience difficulty accessing such service.

pmc-13682166.title: Digital Diabetes Health Coaching for Adults With Uncontrolled Type 2 Diabetes: Protocol for a Scoping Review
pmc-13682166.creator: Fikadu Yehualashet, Adhanom Baraki, Karen Yeates, Catherine Harley, Kevin Woo
pmc-13682166.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundRecent advancements in digital health have enabled the development of technology-enhanced diabetes coaching programs that offer personalized, data-driven, and adaptive support. However, evidence on their implementation and impact is scattered and has not been comprehensively synthesized.
